question: Should Gateway allow scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*` in `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`, or should extension clients be limited to exact non-standard origin allowlisting unless a narrower pattern policy is designed?
rationale: The implementation is small, but the product/security choice changes what browser origins an operator can trust through a stable Gateway config surface.

options.title: Require constrained pattern design
options.body: Approve this direction only with documented matching rules, negative tests, and security guidance for extension-origin trust.

options.title: Keep exact-origin only
options.body: Close or defer scheme wildcards and rely on exact custom-scheme origin matching from the related PRs, accepting the extension-ID config churn.

options.title: Allow raw scheme wildcard
options.body: Permit `chrome-extension://*` directly as an opt-in policy, accepting that any Chrome extension origin can pass the browser-origin check when other auth succeeds.

recommendation.title: Require constrained pattern design
recommendation.body: Approve this direction only with documented matching rules, negative tests, and security guidance for extension-origin trust.

likelyOwner.reason: The original Gateway origin hardening commit is the central product/security boundary this decision would modify.
